deep.reconstruction:
Context and authorship. This page is not a Riemann derivation. It is an editorial draft, almost certainly by H. Weber, of the explanatory note that follows Riemann's Paris prize essay ('Commentatio mathematica', 1861) in the Gesammelte Werke (1876). The page itself says so. The German opening reads: 'This passage can be regarded as a commentary on the lecture "Ueber die Hypothesen ..."; for better understanding we add some things, mostly taken from Dedekind's investigations.' The Latin version reads '... quae maxima ex parte e disquisitionibus excerpta sunt, quas R. Dedekind summa cura instituit.' The mathematics is the construction of Riemann normal (geodesic polar) coordinates. It then derives the conditions that characterise them.

Step 1 (geodesics). Let the metric be ds^2 = sum b_{ii'}(s) ds_i ds_{i'} in n dimensions. Shortest lines, parametrised by arclength r measured from an arbitrary point s^0, satisfy the Euler-Lagrange equations
  d/dr( sum_i b_{mu i} ds_i/dr ) = (1/2) sum_{ii'} (d b_{ii'}/d s_mu) (ds_i/dr)(ds_{i'}/dr),
together with the normalisation sum b_{ii'} (ds_i/dr)(ds_{i'}/dr) = 1.

Step 2 (new coordinates). Put c_i = (ds_i/dr) at r = 0, the initial unit direction, so sum b^0_{ii'} c_i c_{i'} = 1. Define x_i = r c_i; this is the inverse of the exponential map at s^0. The c_i are constant along each geodesic from 0, so each such geodesic is a straight ray x = r c. Write the metric in the new variables as ds^2 = sum a_{ii'}(x) dx_i dx_{i'}.
- Along a ray dx/dr = c, so the unit-speed condition gives sum a_{ii'}(x) c_i c_{i'} = 1.
- At 0 the Jacobian ds/dx is the identity [my filling], so a^0 = b^0 and sum a^0 c c = 1.

Step 3 (geodesic equations in the new coordinates). The equations become d( sum_i a_{mu i} c_i ) = (1/2) dr sum (d a_{ii'}/d x_mu) c_i c_{i'}. Along the ray, the left side equals dr sum_{ii'} (d a_{mu i}/d x_{i'}) c_i c_{i'} [my filling]. Symmetrising in i,i' and multiplying by r^2 gives
  (2)  sum_{ii'} p_{mu i i'} x_i x_{i'} = 0,  where p_{mu i i'} = d a_{i mu}/d x_{i'} + d a_{i' mu}/d x_i - d a_{ii'}/d x_mu.
Here p is twice the Christoffel symbol of the first kind. The equivalent form is sum (d a_{ii'}/d x_mu) x_i x_{i'} = 2 sum (d a_{i mu}/d x_{i'}) x_i x_{i'}. Both are struck through on the page, but the reformulation is kept.

Step 4 (crossed-out reformulation; it reappears in clean form on the next page). Define omega_mu = sum_i a_{mu i} x_i. Then d omega_mu/d x_nu = a_{mu nu} + sum_i (d a_{mu i}/d x_nu) x_i. Hence:
- sum (d a_{ii'}/d x_mu) x_i x_{i'} = sum_i (d omega_i/d x_mu) x_i - omega_mu;
- sum (d a_{mu i}/d x_{i'}) x_i x_{i'} = sum_i (d omega_mu/d x_i) x_i - omega_mu.
Substituting into (2) gives the n first-order PDEs
  (2*)  omega_mu + sum_i (d omega_i/d x_mu) x_i = 2 D omega_mu,  with D = sum x_i d/dx_i the Euler operator.

Step 5. Put 2 omega = sum omega_i x_i = sum a_{ii'} x_i x_{i'}. Then 2 d omega/d x_mu = omega_mu + sum (d omega_i/d x_mu) x_i = 2 D omega_mu, using the commutator d(Du)/dx_nu = du/dx_nu + D(du/dx_nu).
- Differentiating again: d^2 omega/(dx_mu dx_nu) = (1 + D)(d omega_mu/d x_nu).
- By symmetry this also equals (1 + D)(d omega_nu/d x_mu).
- Therefore D Theta = -Theta, with Theta = d omega_mu/d x_nu - d omega_nu/d x_mu.
The page stops here. The next page concludes:
- Theta is homogeneous of degree -1, so if the a's and their derivatives are finite at 0, then Theta = 0;
- consequently omega is homogeneous of degree 2 (the Gauss lemma: sum a x x = sum a^0 x x = r^2);
- finally d a_{ii'}/d x_{i''} = 0 at 0, the characteristic property of normal coordinates.
A struck sentence on this page already anticipates that 2 omega is homogeneous of second order.
errors: No mathematical errors on the page; every displayed identity checks.
The step from the geodesic equation to sum p x x = 0 silently uses dx/dr = c along rays and a symmetrisation. Both are correct.
The claim sum a_{ii'} c c = 1 is justified by unit speed along rays. The claim a^0 = b^0 relies on ds/dx = identity at 0, which is not stated.

The struck-out sentence asserting that 2 omega = sum a x x is homogeneous of degree 2 is true (Gauss lemma). It is not yet justified at that point, which is plausibly why it was deleted and deferred to the next page.
The next page's inference 'homogeneous of degree -1 and finite at 0 implies zero' needs more than finiteness at 0 alone, namely boundedness near 0. That is the standard tacit assumption.

results.what: Geodesic equations, in arclength parametrisation, for a general n-dimensional quadratic line element
Coordinates x_i = r c_i defined by geodesics from a point, so that geodesics through 0 are straight lines; condition sum p_{mu i i'} x_i x_{i'} = 0
results.modern_name: Riemann normal coordinates (characterising condition Gamma_{ij}^k(x) x^i x^j = 0)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Habilitation 1854; Commentatio 1861), elaborated by Dedekind/Weber in the 1876 Werke notes

results.what: Reformulation through omega_mu = sum a_{mu i} x_i and the Euler operator, leading to the homogeneity argument for d omega_mu/dx_nu - d omega_nu/dx_mu
results.modern_name: Gauss lemma / proof that the first derivatives of the metric vanish at the origin of normal coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (2D), Riemann; this proof is Dedekind's, as published in Riemann's Werke (Weber's commentary)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an editorial draft, by Weber after Dedekind, of the published commentary to Riemann's 1861 Commentatio, explicitly attributed on the page to Dedekind. It contains standard normal-coordinate material already printed in the 1876 Werke.

transcription_corrections: The page is an editorial commentary in Weber's hand, citing Dedekind ('quas R. Dedekind summa cura instituit'), not Riemann's own text; the German and Latin headers are two drafts of the same editorial sentence.

The Latin opening reads approximately 'Haec[?] tanquam commentarium ~~eam~~ spectari potest {sunt above} commentationis "Ueber ..."'; the published Werke version is 'tanquam commentarium spectari potest commentationis ...'.
The insertion over 'Geometrie' is likely 'zusammenhängen[?]' and its placement is uncertain; it is an interlinear correction, not part of the title.
In the first struck sentence the reading 'zum grössten Theil aus den Untersuchungen von Dedekind entnommen sind' is correct; 'was die' is an uncorrected grammatical slip in the draft.
The struck equation labelled '2.' and the 'vel ...' line are deleted on the page, but the definition of p_{mu i i'} and the sentence 'unde concluditur, esse sum p x x = 0' are retained.

In 'Tunc fit' the struck fragment above is an aborted d omega/d x_mu; the line reads 2 d omega/d x_mu = omega_mu + sum_i (d omega_i/d x_mu) x_i = 2 D omega_mu, and then d^2 omega/(d x_mu d x_nu) = d omega_mu/d x_nu + D(d omega_mu/d x_nu).
